question: Let $A$ and $B$ be $2 \times 2$ real matrices such that $A+B$ is symmetric, and $A-B$ is skew symmetric. If $A=\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 \\ a & b\end{bmatrix}$, which of the following is true?
explanation:
$A+B$ symmetric $\implies (A+B)' = A+B$
$A-B$ skew symmetric $\implies (A-B)' = -(A-B)$
Let $A = \begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 \\ a & b\end{bmatrix}$.
$A+B$ is symmetric:
So, $A+B = \begin{bmatrix}1+B_{11} & 2+B_{12} \\ a+B_{21} & b+B_{22}\end{bmatrix}$.
It must be equal to its transpose, so $2+B_{12} = a+B_{21}$, $1+B_{11}=b+B_{22}$.
$A-B$ is skew symmetric. $A-B$ = $\begin{bmatrix}1-B_{11} & 2-B_{12} \\ a-B_{21} & b-B_{22}\end{bmatrix}$.
Its transpose $= \begin{bmatrix} 1-B_{11} & a-B_{21} \\ 2-B_{12} & b-B_{22} \end{bmatrix}$.
So, $a-B_{21} = -(2-B_{12}) \implies a-B_{21} = -2+B_{12}$
$2-B_{12} = -(a-B_{21})$
Simplifying, $a=-2$, $b=1$
So, (B) is correct.
